benchmark.category: an open-world GTA-style single-file browser game set on a college campus
benchmark.users: hackathon judges and student players who open the preview link on desktop and on their own phones to play the five daily campus missions and meet the story characters

requirements.source_phrase: catch the voice and place it
requirements.statement: In Adhiraj's office scenes every fixed line — the openers, the mid-beat reactions, the apologies, the closings and the brushoff — is heard in the cloned voice made from the uploaded recording, audible and non-empty, with no fixed line still played by the old stand-in voice
requirements.notes: Replaces the stand-in-only contract of this requirement with the cloned voice the user supplied and approved. Browsers block audio before a gesture, so the office must be entered by a key press or tap first; the caller checks audible playback and no console error, not just that markup exists.

requirements.source_phrase: Keep the stand-in voice for those
requirements.statement: The stand-in voice path is kept for office lines whose text carries a teammate's name or the visit number, and for any fixed line whose clip is missing or fails to load; each line plays exactly one source, the clip or the stand-in but never both, and the fallback yields a non-empty utterance or its subtitle so the scene advances instead of hanging
requirements.notes: From the user's answer on how lines with a teammate's name or a visit number should sound; the missing-clip half is the paranoid form so a 404 or an empty file cannot dead-end the scene, and the one-source rule catches clip and speech synthesis playing over each other.

requirements.source_phrase: catch the voice and place it
requirements.statement: The served game maps each of the 25 fixed office line ids (open-1..open-5, mid-1..mid-9, apo-1..apo-4, again-2, again-3, close-long, close-quiet, close-apo, close-default, brushoff) to assets/adhiraj/<id>.mp3, and each of those URLs returns 200 or 206 with Content-Type audio/mpeg and non-zero bytes, so no fixed office line plays from a missing or empty file
requirements.notes: The 25 ids come from the build description (files_of_reference /app/frontend/public/game/assets/adhiraj/*.mp3). Fetch each file directly to prove it is served non-empty; a clip that 404s would silently fall back and hide the missing voice.

requirements.source_phrase: Make sure he says the same thing as in the current game; only the voice changes to the attached one.
requirements.statement: Every office line's on-screen text — the opener, the mid-beat reactions, the choice replies and the closing line — reads exactly as it did before the voice change, and that text is on screen while its audio plays
requirements.notes: The user forbids content changes; a line whose subtitle was rewritten to match the recording's original words fails this. Compare against the pre-change DIR_* strings, not against the audio.

requirements.source_phrase: Make sure he says the same thing as in the current game; only the voice changes to the attached one.
requirements.statement: The served index.html still holds the DIR_OPEN, DIR_MID, DIR_REACT and dirClosing strings unchanged from before the voice change, and each clip id the generation script lists corresponds to that line's text
requirements.notes: The line text per id is listed in /app/scripts/adhiraj_voice.py; character-exact comparison of the strings is mechanical, while the audio-to-text correspondence needs a listening check and is the hard half.

requirements.source_phrase: only the voice changes to the attached one
requirements.statement: Entering the office, choosing Apologise, Blame or Say nothing at each beat, hearing a closing line and leaving the office follow the same sequence, choices, rewards and star clearing as before, with only the audio changed
requirements.notes: The user's change limit; the risk is that swapping the voice path rewrote beat logic or dropped a branch.

requirements.source_phrase: only the voice changes to the attached one
requirements.statement: dirEnter, dirChoose and dirClosing keep the same branches, rewards and wanted-star clearing as before the voice change, with the only code difference on the voice playback path
requirements.notes: Read the office functions in the served file and diff the beat table against the pre-change version; judge by branches and reward values, not by formatting.

requirements.source_phrase: Keep the stand-in voice for those
requirements.statement: An office line whose text contains a teammate's name or the visit number is heard through the browser stand-in voice with its text on screen, and the scene moves on to the next beat without hanging
requirements.notes: The user's explicit exception; the failure it guards is a blame reaction or blame closing that selects no clip and then never resolves, leaving the scene stuck.

requirements.statement: With at least one wanted star, entering the office plays an opener, accepts a choice at each beat, plays a closing line after Leave the office is chosen, returns to free play with the wanted stars cleared, and every line's typewriter text finishes so the scene cannot stall, with no uncaught JS error
requirements.notes: Build description: office entry needs wantedLevel()>=1 and the scene runs open → mid → close with typewriter text. The continuity note gives the page.evaluate shortcut (S.stars=2; S.dirT=-999; dirEnter()) for reaching the office quickly.

requirements.statement: dirEnter with wantedLevel() >= 1 advances the scene through the beats to a closing line, dirChoose records the option picked at each beat, leaving resets the office state so the next visit starts fresh and clears the wanted stars, and no pageerror is raised during the flow
requirements.notes: Check the office flags and wanted level after leaving, not only the on-screen card; a flag left set is the softlock the user reported for other scenes.

requirements.statement: Entering the office with zero wanted stars plays the brushoff line and no reaction or closing line, then returns the player to free play, on desktop and on a phone
requirements.notes: Build description: with 0 stars dirEnter() plays the brushoff ('Do you need something?'); the item exercises that clip file in the shipped voice set.

requirements.statement: dirEnter with wantedLevel() === 0 selects the brushoff clip and runs no reaction or closing branch, leaving the wanted level and the stored save unchanged
requirements.notes: The brushoff path was previously the whole feature; the risk is the new voice code running beats even at 0 stars.

requirements.statement: The second office visit plays the again-2 opener and the third plays again-3, each with its own text, and the visit count survives a page reload so the same opener is heard again after reloading
requirements.notes: Build description: again-2 and again-3 are the second and third visit openers and S.dirUses counts visits. Two visits in one session and one after a reload are both needed.

requirements.statement: The save's office visit counter increments once per office entry, is read back after a reload, and selects again-2 on visit 2 and again-3 on visit 3 while visit 4 and later fall through to the visit-number line rather than replaying a fixed opener
requirements.notes: Guards against a counter that increments per beat (skipping again-2 to a later opener) or resets on reload.

requirements.statement: While an office clip is playing the voice label beside the scene reads 'his voice (AI-recreated)', and the label names no other speaker during that playback
requirements.notes: Build description: #ofvoice shows 'his voice (AI-recreated)' while a clip plays; the user's permission answer is what the 'AI-recreated' wording credits.

requirements.statement: The served markup contains 'his voice (AI-recreated)' bound to the #ofvoice label, set when a clip starts and cleared or returned to its idle text when the clip ends
requirements.notes: Character-exact string check plus a check the label is not permanently stuck on after the scene ends.

requirements.statement: Pause menu → Audio mixer shows a note stating that Adhiraj's voice is an AI recreation made with his permission
requirements.notes: Build description: the mixer note (~5155) mentions the AI recreation made with permission; the user answered 'Yes, he has agreed' to the consent question, which is what the note records in the product.

requirements.statement: The served markup for the audio mixer panel contains that note text naming the AI recreation and the permission, and the panel still opens from the pause menu with the game's other sound settings
requirements.notes: String check on the served file; keep the mixer otherwise unchanged so the note does not replace the volume controls.

requirements.statement: Adhiraj's voice is created with Emergent managed voice cloning and the 25 clips are shipped inside the served app, so playing an office line makes no request to an external voice service and needs no key or credential
requirements.notes: The user chose the service; the build description (other_misc_info) says the cloning is pre-generated with no runtime API. Test by loading the office with network calls to outside hosts blocked after page load — the scene must still be voiced.

requirements.statement: Every voiced office line shows its subtitle text while the audio plays, and setting the mixer's voice volume to zero silences the line while the scene still advances through its beats
requirements.notes: benchmark: dialogue-driven browser games always subtitle voiced lines and put their volume under the game's own audio mixer, so a player with sound off or on a muted phone can follow the scene.

requirements.statement: Each clip's playback is routed through the mixer's voice gain node or volume setting, so a zeroed voice volume produces silence for the clip without blocking line advance, and muting the other channels leaves the voice audible
requirements.notes: benchmark: dialogue-driven browser games — a voice channel the mixer does not control, or one that stalls the scene when muted, is the usual bug.

requirements.statement: The campus map shows each of today's uncompleted missions as a coloured dot labelled with that mission's name, and a mission already completed today has no dot
requirements.notes: Build description: the map now marks uncompleted daily missions as coloured dots with their names. Distinct from the inherited active-mission marker on the minimap.

requirements.statement: The map reads each mission's position and today's completion state from the mission table and the save, so a dot disappears once its mission is completed and stays gone after a reload
requirements.notes: Check the dot list against the five mission positions and the saved completion marks, not only that dots render.

requirements.statement: Switching tabs or taking a call during The Pitch pauses the beat sequence, and on return the remaining beats play on from where they stopped with none counted as missed for the time away
requirements.notes: Build description: the pitch now pauses when the tab is hidden, fixing a lose-your-mission bug. Simulate with document.hidden / a tab switch and check the beat index and the mission outcome.

requirements.statement: The Pitch's beat scheduler stops advancing while the page is hidden and resumes at the same beat when the page becomes visible, so its outcome matches an uninterrupted run
requirements.notes: A paused pitch that still decrements its own timer would expire while hidden; compare the mission result with and without a hidden interval of the same length.

requirements.statement: The Yulu Time Trial result shows the run's leaderboard rank as a whole number of at least 1 and never as '#0', including for a slow run
requirements.notes: Build description: a slower run used to display rank '#0' and now shows the correct rank; test with a deliberately slow finish.

requirements.statement: The rank is computed from the run's recorded time against the stored leaderboard times and clamped to at least 1, so a slower run shows a lower rank rather than zero
requirements.notes: Business-logic class on the mission result; the seeded times must be compared, since a single run has no position among zero competitors.

requirements.statement: At 390x844 portrait the running mission's countdown is fully readable near the top of the screen and is not covered by the mission card, the stick or the action buttons
requirements.notes: Build description: on upright phones the countdown now sits near the top because it used to sit behind the mission card. Layout check with a mission running.

requirements.statement: The portrait CSS places the mission timer above the mission card in the stacking order and inside the viewport at 390x844 and 360x640
requirements.notes: Check the computed stacking/z-index and the timer's bounding box against the mission card's at both viewports; a rule that only applies in landscape would leave portrait broken.
